rationale.conceptual: The heat-flow simulation uses an established FEM method (heat equation) with known material properties and equations (thermo-optic relation) from the paper. The geometry (silicon pillar + silica toroid) is non-trivial to model correctly, requiring proper meshing and boundary conditions, but no novel algorithm is invented. This is a careful, multi-part implementation of a documented approach, fitting a conceptual level of 3 (established but non-trivial method).
rationale.execution: The workflow consists of a few sequential stages (model setup, steady-state solves, shift conversion, transient solve, cutoff extraction) that can be implemented in a single Python script using FEniCS. There is no complicated multi-file orchestration or heavy data assembly; the only external resource is the paper's supplementary PDF. The pipeline is simple, making execution difficulty low (2).

The execution pipeline is straightforward (single script, two output files). Resource needs are very low: small FEM runs on CPU with minimal memory.
